title: Postmortem: HPA/KEDA autoscaling regression causing false positives and cold-start spikes
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Summary:
During a traffic surge on 2026-02-17 we observed repeated capacity events where the autoscaling layer (HPA + KEDA) incorrectly scaled down critical inference pods, then triggered rapid scale-ups producing a wave of cold-starts. This produced elevated tail latency for streaming and chat routes and increased token-cost by ~18% for affected customers.

What happened (high level):
- At 09:15 UTC an upstream burst of short-lived requests (many <100ms) increased request-per-pod variance.
- KEDA's external scaler metric pipeline filtered noisy signals incorrectly after a recent change to the metric aggregation window (PR: infra/metrics#719).
- HPA interpreted the absence of sustained high CPU as opportunity to scale down. Combined with fast scale-down TTL we observed pods terminate while KV caches were still warming.
- Subsequent scale-ups hit cold-start time and warming overhead; autoscaling oscillated for ~27 minutes until manual override.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency SLO breaches for 11 customers for 27 minutes.
- Increased token consumption and cost due to repeated regenerate calls for streaming clients.
- No data loss or security exposure.

Root causes (evidence):
- Regression introduced in infra/metrics PR #719 changed KEDA metricAggregationWindowSeconds from 30s to 5s to try to reduce detection latency; this amplified short-lived bursts into scale triggers (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/719).
- HPA verticalScaleDownStabilizationSeconds was set to 30s for some deployments but not all; mismatch created asymmetric scale-down behavior across clusters.
- Runbook lacked explicit guidance for toggling metricAggregationWindowSeconds and lacked a rollback knob in the KEDA helm values.

Mitigation taken during incident:
- 09:45 UTC: Ops increased desired replicas to a safe minimum to stop further scale-downs.
- 10:02 UTC: Rolled back metricAggregationWindowSeconds change in staging; validated with load tests.
- 10:27 UTC: Re-enabled progressive scale-down stabilization and added an emergency feature-flag to KEDA helm chart to ignore the external scaler temporarily.

Longer-term fixes and action items are captured below with owners and ETA.
action_items: A1: Add a KEDA helm value 'metricAggregationWindowSeconds' with a safe default and document trade-offs (owner: Ava Chen, due: 2026-03-05)
A2: Update HPA stabilization settings to use consistent scaleDown/scaleUp stabilization windows across clusters and add tests (owner: Diego Martinez, due: 2026-03-10)
A3: Implement a circuit-breaker flag in the Console to toggle external scalers per-cluster for emergency ops (owner: Priya Singh, due: 2026-03-19)
A4: Add a chaos-y test harness in staging to simulate short-lived request bursts and validate autoscaler behavior (owner: Backend QA, due: 2026-03-26)
A5: Instrument a new KEDA metric 'keda.noise_ratio' and dashboard to alert on noisy signal amplification (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-12)
A6: Revise runbook: include exact rollback steps for recent metrics PRs, include playbook for emergency desiredReplica override, and add post-incident checklist (owner: Samir Patel, due: 2026-03-01)
A7: Add automated pre-merge gating: run load pattern simulation for infra/metrics changes that touch aggregation windows (owner: CI team, due: 2026-04-02)
A8: Quantify cost impact and notify affected customers with summary and credits if requested (owner: Customer Success, due: 2026-03-08)
A9: Evaluate migration to per-route adaptive caching to reduce cold-start penalty for chat/streaming endpoints (owner: Runtime team, due: 2026-04-09)
comments: 2026-02-17 09:52 UTC - Ava Chen: Scaled desired replicas to 12 to halt oscillation. Confirmed tail latency dropping after warming.
2026-02-17 10:12 UTC - Samir Patel: Rolled back metricAggregationWindowSeconds change in infra repo; will run canary tests in staging.
2026-02-18 11:03 UTC - Diego Martinez: Began audit of HPA stabilization settings across clusters; found two clusters with missing settings.
2026-02-22 16:40 UTC - Priya Singh: Prototype of console toggle implemented; needs UX review before release.
2026-03-01 09:15 UTC - Customer Success: Preparing customer notifications and list of affected accounts for credits discussion.
notes: Key technical trade-off: reducing aggregation window improves detection latency for sustained ramps but increases sensitivity to microbursts. For customer-facing inference workloads we prioritize stabilization and cache-warmth over sub-10s detection latency. Action A1/A2 codify that priority.
